proposed.en: a sixtier, one of the Soviet-style idealists of the sixties
proposed.zh: 六十年代理想主义者（苏联‘六十年代人’）

terms.gloss: Apple's famous '1984' Super Bowl ad (Ridley Scott), casting IBM as Orwell's Big Brother.
terms.why_hard: Reader must connect it to the very next clause about fighting IBM; translating just as 'the 1984 ad' without the Orwell/Apple frame loses the rebellion theme of the whole passage.

terms.gloss: Apple's self-image as pirates (the original pirate flag over the Mac team's building), rebels against the establishment.
terms.why_hard: The pirate metaphor runs through the book's portrait of VK as rebels; must keep the flag lore implicit, not turn into 'hacker'.

proposed.ja: アップルは海賊だった

terms.gloss: IBM, transliterated into Russian slang and called 'rotten' — Apple's old enemy cast as decayed.
terms.why_hard: Both the russified transliteration and the 'rotten' register matter: Durov speaks of IBM as something gone off, an epithet repeated in 'тухлый дизайн' below.

terms.gloss: Parody of Soviet bureaucratic phraseology: a product 'capturing broad strata of the population', i.e. mass-market takeover told in party-speak.
terms.why_hard: The joke is the register — Soviet propaganda clichés describing Apple marketing; a straight business rendering ('mass adoption') kills the irony.

proposed.en: The product's conquest of the broad masses of the population
proposed.zh: 产品对广大人民群众的占领
proposed.ja: 製品による広範な人民層の制圧

terms.gloss: Durov's recurring enemy-list: 'rotten design' and 'wholesale monetisation', the same decay vocabulary as his IBM jibe.
terms.why_hard: The decay metaphors (тухлый/протухший) must be consistent with the IBM epithet above, and 'повальная' (an epidemic of monetisation) should keep the plague register.

proposed.en: putrid design and the monetisation craze
proposed.zh: 腐臭的设计与泛滥的变现
proposed.ja: 腐ったデザインと全面化したマネタイズ

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte, the book's subject
terms.why_hard: Must stay the same surname form as the rest of the book, never 'Duroff' or given-name-only

terms.gloss: Durov's apartment on Sennaya (Haymarket) Square, central St Petersburg
terms.why_hard: Сенная is a toponym, not 'hay square' calqued; must match other Sennaya mentions

terms.gloss: Sennaya Square / Haymarket district in St Petersburg
terms.why_hard: Transliteration vs translation (Haymarket) would split the map for readers

terms.gloss: the downside/worst-case path of events, startup-speak of the era
terms.why_hard: Calquing 'negative scenario' sounds like film; it is risk-talk, not cinema

proposed.ja: ネガティブ・シナリオ

terms.term: ты на самом деле ничем не владеешь
terms.gloss: you don't really own anything (stoic/memento-mori ownership line)
terms.why_hard: владеешь is legal-own, not 'have'; flattening it loses the property-rights sting

proposed.zh: 你其实什么都不真正拥有
proposed.ja: 実際には何も所有していない

terms.term: потерять то, что у тебя якобы есть
terms.gloss: be ready to lose what you only supposedly possess
terms.why_hard: якобы marks illusory possession; 'supposedly' vs 'allegedly' changes tone

proposed.en: lose what you only supposedly have
proposed.zh: 失去你自以为拥有的东西
proposed.ja: あると思い込んでいるものを失う

terms.term: ветхие мехи прохудятся и вино выльется само
terms.gloss: allusion to new wine bursting old wineskins (Gospels); old vessels fail and the wine spills of itself
terms.why_hard: Must stay recognizably biblical, not a random leaky-bag image; 'wineskins' not 'fur'

proposed.en: the old wineskins will split and the wine will spill of itself
proposed.zh: 旧皮袋终会裂开，酒自己就会流出来
proposed.ja: 古い革袋が破れてワインが自ら流れ出す

terms.gloss: old wineskins: worn institutions/containers that cannot hold the new
terms.why_hard: мехи is wineskins, not 'bellows' or 'fur coats', a common dictionary trap

terms.gloss: politics no longer manufactures compelling leaders
terms.why_hard: производит is industrial 'produce', not 'elect'; keep the factory metaphor

proposed.en: Politics does not produce interesting leaders
proposed.zh: 政治生产不出有意思的领袖
proposed.ja: 政治は面白い指導者を生み出さない

terms.gloss: Durov's label for founders who build mass civic products and thereby enter politics
terms.why_hard: Keep the English coinage or it becomes generic CSR/'stakeholder capitalism'

proposed.ja: アクティビスト・キャピタリズム

terms.gloss: shift in the information paradigm (how news/social data flow)
terms.why_hard: парадигма is Kuhn-lite tech talk, not 'information model' or 'media format'

terms.term: со всей возможной в четыре утра ясностью
terms.gloss: with all the clarity possible at four in the morning (exhausted-interview irony)
terms.why_hard: Keep the clock time; 'dawn' or 'late night' loses the 4 a.m. reportage beat

proposed.en: with all the clarity possible at four in the morning
proposed.zh: 在凌晨四点所能有的全部清醒里
proposed.ja: 午前四時に可能な限りの明晰さで

terms.gloss: The streams of people dried up — the crowds thinned as if a river ran dry, but only for two hours.
terms.why_hard: A literal rendering ('human flows dried') is incomprehensible; the river-drying image must be kept while making clear it means the crowd dispersed.

proposed.en: the streams of people ran dry

terms.gloss: Ironic epithet: Durov is likened to a seagull, a scruffy, opportunist St Petersburg bird; also echoes Chekhov's 'Seagull' emblem of the tortured creator.
terms.why_hard: Missing the seagull simile turns a sharp comic image into a plain description; it may also be a recurring epithet for Durov across the book.

proposed.en: a seagull by the name of Pavel Durov
proposed.zh: 一只名叫帕维尔·杜罗夫的海鸥
proposed.ja: パベル・ドゥーロフという名のカモメ

terms.gloss: Lurching along with one shoulder higher — a lopsided, self-important strut.
terms.why_hard: Flat 'walking crookedly' loses the mocking caricature of the entrepreneur's pose; this matches the 'seagull' satire and must stay comic.

terms.gloss: A French-style jacket with foam-padded shoulders — the uniform of 1990s Russian 'new Russians'/biznesmeny, deliberately oversized and comical.
terms.why_hard: Rendering as 'a coat with padded shoulders' loses the instantly recognisable 90s-gangster connotation for a Russian reader; needs an analogue, not a description.

proposed.en: a trench coat with foam-padded shoulders
proposed.zh: 垫着海绵厚肩的九十年代老板式大衣
proposed.ja: スポンジの肩パッドの入った90年代風ビジネスジャケット

terms.gloss: 'The new vine-growers' — the incoming generation of tech entrepreneurs who tend and reshape society; biblical/parable overtones of being given a new vineyard.
terms.why_hard: A literal 'new winemakers' reads as a non sequitur; the parable-like register (stewards of a new crop) must survive, and the phrase may recur as a book-level motif.

proposed.ja: 新しい葡萄園の耕し手

terms.gloss: Entrepreneurs now rival politicians, the state, and academia as producers of intellectual capacity — 'академия' means the academic world, not a specific school.
terms.why_hard: 'The academy' could be misread as a particular institution (e.g. an academy of sciences); it is the generic scholarly estate.

proposed.en: compete with politicians, the state, and academia
proposed.zh: 与政客、国家和学术界竞争
proposed.ja: 政治家や国家、アカデミアと競合する

terms.gloss: The colonnade of a St Petersburg hotel (in context, a landmark entrance where fans gathered — likely the Astoria near St Isaac's Square).
terms.why_hard: An unidentified 'hotel colonnade' disorients readers; translators must fix which hotel and keep its name consistent if it appears later in the book.

terms.gloss: The worn-out idols the fans are waiting for — earlier internet-era heroes (likely the older generation of web celebrities); 'кумир' carries pop-worship weight.
terms.why_hard: 'Old idols' can read as antiques or age; it means has-been celebrities of a previous wave, with a note of pity.

proposed.en: the idols of an earlier age

terms.gloss: A cardboard fan sign used as an umbrella — the standard fan-held placard at Russian public appearances.
terms.why_hard: 'Cardboard poster' should convey the makeshift fan placard (with a slogan for the idol), not a printed advertisement.

proposed.ja: 段ボール製の応援ボード

terms.gloss: first-year student, main developer of VK's Android app
terms.why_hard: real person's name transliteration must stay consistent across mentions

proposed.zh: 格里高利·克留什尼科夫
proposed.ja: グリゴリー・クリュシニコフ

terms.gloss: VKontakte, Russian social network founded by Durov
terms.why_hard: must use official branding consistently, not translate literally

terms.gloss: reference to a developer contest for VK's Android app
terms.why_hard: need to render as recognizable tech/product context, not overly literal

terms.gloss: guys obsessed/into mobile apps, period tech slang
terms.why_hard: casual slang 'угорать по' (to be really into something) needs equivalent register without sounding archaic

proposed.ja: モバイルアプリに熱中している

terms.gloss: slicked-back, mafia-looking men (visual stereotype of 2000s Russian business/crime elite)
terms.why_hard: cultural stereotype of post-Soviet 'mafiosi' look must be conveyed without literal 'mafia man' sounding cartoonish

proposed.zh: 梳得油光水滑的黑帮分子
proposed.ja: 髪を撫でつけたマフィアのような男たち

terms.gloss: shadowy figures in tailcoats and low-cut dresses, evoking hotel lobby elite ambiance
terms.why_hard: poetic register describing anonymous elegant crowd, easy to flatten into plain description

proposed.zh: 燕尾服与低胸礼服的身影
proposed.ja: 燕尾服とイブニングドレスの人影

terms.gloss: dumping, selling below value/market price
terms.why_hard: economic term used metaphorically for selling out cheaply; must keep consistent economic connotation

terms.gloss: "slavery, fleeing the battlefield" — Durov's metaphor for selling his stake
terms.why_hard: must preserve the martial/moral metaphor tone Durov is known for, not soften it

proposed.ja: 奴隷であり、戦場からの逃亡だ

terms.gloss: "not the Russian way" — appeal to national character/pride
terms.why_hard: carries implicit nationalist/cultural pride connotation that a flat translation loses

proposed.zh: 这不是俄罗斯人的做法

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte
terms.why_hard: surname alone must consistently refer to Pavel, not confused with brother Nikolai elsewhere in book

terms.gloss: first-year university student (implies youth, SPbU context)
terms.why_hard: conveys Russian university year system; should stay consistent with other academic-year references in book

terms.gloss: VKontakte's in-house coders/developers, salary benchmark
terms.why_hard: term 'кодеры' should be rendered consistently as 'coders/developers' throughout the book

terms.gloss: VKontakte, the Russian social network founded by Pavel Durov.
terms.why_hard: Book-wide decision: keep transliteration 'VKontakte' vs use 'VK', and quote-mark conventions differ by language.

terms.gloss: Mail.ru Group, the Russian internet holding company that owned Odnoklassniki and competed with VK.
terms.why_hard: Often conflated with the mail service; here it means the whole holding (холдинг), a distinction to keep consistent.

terms.gloss: Odnoklassniki ('Classmates'), the social network owned by Mail.ru, VK's main rival.
terms.why_hard: Literal translation ('Classmates') vs brand name; must match usage across the whole book.

terms.gloss: Ilya Shirokov, head of Odnoklassniki (and later Mail.ru's social-media arm) at the time.
terms.why_hard: A minor figure whose name and role must be checked; readers won't know who he is without a whisper of context.

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte and the book's subject.
terms.why_hard: Surname-only references are fine in Russian; some target languages need the full name at first mention per book-wide convention.

terms.gloss: The Singer House, the famous Art Nouveau building on Nevsky Prospect that housed VK's St Petersburg office.
terms.why_hard: A metonym for VK itself; translating it literally as 'Zingel's house' or keeping only 'Singer House' loses the metonymy unless handled consistently everywhere it appears.

proposed.ja: シンガー・ハウス（VK本社）

terms.gloss: The blue and orange lines of a traffic-growth chart — blue for VK, orange for Odnoklassniki (their brand colors).
terms.why_hard: The color-to-company mapping is implicit; a reader (or translator) may miss that the colors are the companies' brand colors and the rivalry is drawn as a race between two curves.

proposed.en: the blue line (VK) / the orange line (Odnoklassniki)
proposed.ja: 青い線（VK）とオレンジの線（Odnoklassniki）

terms.gloss: The 'war' between Mail.ru and VKontakte — a recurring frame in the book for the two companies' rivalry.
terms.why_hard: An extended military metaphor (война, фронт, затишье, колкости) running through the book that must be kept coherent, not translated piecemeal.

terms.gloss: Snide remarks, barbed exchanges between the two companies in the press.
terms.why_hard: Register: 'exchanged pleasantries' would invert the irony; must convey mockery, not politeness.

terms.gloss: Lull in the hostilities — part of the book's war metaphor.
terms.why_hard: Should keep the military register ('lull before the storm') so the recurring metaphor stays intact.

terms.gloss: Mail.ru was thought to be plotting a move that would bring the Singer House (VK) crashing down in ruins.
terms.why_hard: Mixed with the 'house' metonym: 'reduce the house to ruins' collapses company and building deliberately; flattening it to 'destroy VK' loses the image.

proposed.en: reduce the Singer House to rubble
proposed.ja: シンガー・ハウスを廃墟に変える

terms.gloss: A pouf / floor cushion — a beanbag-style seat typical of casual startup offices.
terms.why_hard: Small but scene-setting: signals the informal dot-com office culture of Odnoklassniki versus VK's grandeur; some languages lack a neat everyday word.

terms.gloss: A glassed-in section of the Odnoklassniki office where programmers and designers sat at school-style desks.
terms.why_hard: The school-desk image (парты) is a deliberate ironic touch — adults at school desks; translators may normalize to 'workstations' and lose it.

proposed.en: glass-walled section, seated at school desks
proposed.zh: 玻璃隔间里，程序员和设计师坐在课桌前
proposed.ja: ガラス張りの区画で、課桌のような机に向かう

terms.gloss: Odnoklassniki's gaming platform (open API for third-party social games, like Facebook's).
terms.why_hard: Period term from 2010–2012 social-gaming boom; must not be rendered as 'game console' or vague 'games service'; consistency with how VK's own platform is described elsewhere.

proposed.ja: ゲームプラットフォーム

terms.gloss: Hit games — the top-grossing social games on the platform.
terms.why_hard: Industry slang; 'hits' must read as games, not pop songs.

terms.gloss: Informal Russian internet slang for 'users' (from English).
terms.why_hard: Register marker of Russian IT-speak of the era; a formal 'users' in the target loses the colloquial tone, but forcing slang may sound dated.

terms.gloss: Odnoklassniki's in-house audio and video hosting services.
terms.why_hard: Hyphenated pair of period tech terms; 'hosting' must stay technical (streaming/storage services), not 'websites'.

proposed.ja: 音声・動画ホスティング

terms.gloss: The two curves would spark on touching — i.e., the rivals were about to clash head-on.
terms.why_hard: Image continuation of the chart metaphor; literal 'sparkle' in some languages reads as celebratory rather than as collision/contact.

proposed.en: sparks would fly the moment they touched
proposed.zh: 两条线一相触便会火花四溅
proposed.ja: 触れ合った瞬間、火花が散るだろう

terms.gloss: Twitter the microblogging service, 2013-era brand
terms.why_hard: Keep period brand; later X rebrand would anachronize the scene

terms.gloss: Durov’s insulting epithet for Mail.ru Group as a trash/tacky holding
terms.why_hard: трэш is 2000s RU internet slang (trashy, low-rent), not English trash as garbage

proposed.ja: 俗悪ホールディングスMail.ru

terms.gloss: Mail.ru Group, Moscow internet conglomerate later VK/VK Company parent
terms.why_hard: Must stay Mail.ru not VK; legal name and era branding matter

terms.gloss: VKontakte social network, Durov’s company
terms.why_hard: Quotes and spelling VK vs VKontakte vs ВКонтакте must be book-wide

terms.gloss: the middle-finger gesture in the restaurant photo Durov tweeted
terms.why_hard: English loan already in source; translating the word vs naming the gesture splits tone

terms.gloss: Russian and international wire services / news agencies
terms.why_hard: not ‘information agencies’; means news wires picking up the tweet

terms.gloss: Dmitry Grishin, Mail.ru Group CEO
terms.why_hard: surname-only; first mention in book must match established full name

terms.gloss: Mail.ru executive (Shirokov) in talks with the author
terms.why_hard: obscure surname; inconsistent romanization would split one person

terms.gloss: publicly listed company constrained by disclosure and PR
terms.why_hard: публичная ≠ ‘public company’ in the civic sense; listing status is the point

terms.gloss: street-thug / chav with a high IQ; Mail.ru managers’ verdict on Durov
terms.why_hard: гопник is untranslatable class/crime subculture, not simply ‘thug’

proposed.en: a gopnik with a high IQ

terms.gloss: Forbes magazine (Russian edition implied)
terms.why_hard: keep Latin brand; Russian Forbes vs US Forbes rarely distinguished in text

terms.gloss: Valery Igumenov, Forbes journalist interviewing Streshinsky
terms.why_hard: romanization of Игуменов (Igumenov vs Igumenoff) must be unique

proposed.ja: ヴァレリー・イグメノフ

terms.gloss: Ivan Streshinsky, Usmanov’s internet lieutenant
terms.why_hard: Стрешинский vs Streshinsky/Streschinsky; role needs research

proposed.ja: イワン・ストレシンスキー

terms.gloss: Alisher Usmanov, oligarch investor behind Mail.ru’s VK bid
terms.why_hard: genitive; book must already have settled Usmanov spelling and titles

terms.gloss: courteous bows / lip-service compliments before the criticism
terms.why_hard: French loan via Russian; literal curtsy would be comic

terms.gloss: flip the main breaker and walk: Durov could kill VK’s infra and leave
terms.why_hard: рубильник is a Soviet knife-switch, not a light switch; keep industrial image

proposed.en: throw the main switch and walk away
proposed.ja: ブレーカーを落として去る

terms.gloss: The Russian social-networking service founded by Pavel Durov, commonly branded VKontakte at the time.
terms.why_hard: Its historical name, modern brand VK, and literal meaning “In Contact” must not be mixed inconsistently.

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder and chief executive of VKontakte.
terms.why_hard: The surname alone should follow the project-wide form chosen for his full name.

terms.gloss: Corporate jargon for the additional value supposedly created by combining businesses.
terms.why_hard: The quotation marks signal investor-speak and Durov's skepticism, not a neutral claim of cooperation.

terms.gloss: A colloquial reference to St Petersburg's higher-education institute for film, photography, and television.
terms.why_hard: A literal “cinema-photo institute” obscures the particular institution and its familiar local nickname.

proposed.en: the Institute of Film and Television
proposed.ja: サンクトペテルブルク映画テレビ大学

terms.gloss: The Fontanka, the central St Petersburg river and embankment district toward which Durov was walking.
terms.why_hard: Russian uses the river name metonymically; the context may mean the river or its embankment rather than a neighborhood.

terms.gloss: Black official luxury cars fitted with flashing priority lights, emblematic of Russia's political and business elite.
terms.why_hard: Rendering them merely as cars with beacons loses the period association with privilege and exemption from traffic rules.

proposed.en: black official cars with flashing blue lights
proposed.zh: 装着特权警灯的黑色官车
proposed.ja: 優先通行灯を点滅させた黒塗りの公用車

terms.gloss: Literally the nobility, used ironically here for the powerful officials and magnates traveling to the reception.
terms.why_hard: A literal historical “nobility” would imply aristocratic titles rather than a sarcastic description of today's elite.

terms.gloss: Alisher Usmanov, a Russian-Uzbek billionaire investor with major interests in Mail.ru Group and other assets.
terms.why_hard: His role in VKontakte, Mail.ru Group, and Gazprom-linked holdings is necessary to understand why he arranged the meeting.

proposed.ja: アリシェル・ウスマノフ

terms.gloss: The St Petersburg International Economic Forum, Russia's major annual government-backed business gathering.
terms.why_hard: The shortened local reference can be mistaken for an unspecified city forum rather than the established SPIEF event.

proposed.en: the St Petersburg International Economic Forum
proposed.zh: 圣彼得堡国际经济论坛
proposed.ja: サンクトペテルブルク国際経済フォーラム

terms.gloss: The Sheremetev Palace, also known as the Fountain House, a historic palace on the Fontanka in St Petersburg.
terms.why_hard: It must not be confused with Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport or other Sheremetev family estates.

proposed.ja: シェレメーチェフ宮殿

terms.gloss: The Russian internet company and portal whose group sought greater control of VKontakte.
terms.why_hard: The period-specific company styling must be distinguished from the mail.ru website and the later VK corporate name.

terms.gloss: An oligarch: an exceptionally wealthy businessman whose power and assets are closely entangled with the Russian state.
terms.why_hard: A generic “billionaire” loses the specifically post-Soviet political and economic connotations.

terms.gloss: Was still acquiring and consolidating business assets for the benefit of Gazprom.
terms.why_hard: The dative construction means gathering assets on Gazprom's behalf, not collecting Gazprom itself or merely owning its shares.

proposed.en: was still assembling assets for Gazprom
proposed.zh: 当时仍在为俄罗斯天然气工业股份公司收拢资产
proposed.ja: なおもガスプロムのために資産を買い集めていた

terms.gloss: Gazprom, Russia's state-controlled natural-gas giant and a central corporate power base.
terms.why_hard: Its political importance and standard international name should be preserved rather than translated generically as a gas company.

proposed.zh: 俄罗斯天然气工业股份公司

terms.gloss: The London Stock Exchange, where the holding company's market valuation was reflected in traded securities.
terms.why_hard: The shorthand denotes the specific exchange, not the London financial market in general.

terms.gloss: VKontakte, characterized as the leading social network across the Russian-speaking internet.
terms.why_hard: “Russian-language” describes its user sphere rather than legal nationality, while “No. 1” is a journalistic ranking claim.

proposed.zh: 俄语互联网第一大社交平台

terms.gloss: Earlier stunt of throwing banknotes into the air (Durov-era VK party lore)
terms.why_hard: Literal 'flights of banknotes' loses the specific prank; must match earlier chapters

proposed.ja: 紙幣を撒き散らす余興

terms.gloss: Play-acting as Neo from The Matrix (or Matrix-themed games) at those parties
terms.why_hard: Нео could be misread as a Russian name or a video game title, not the Matrix avatar

terms.gloss: Wet-T-shirt contests at the same parties
terms.why_hard: Calque as 'wet undershirts' misses the Western contest; must stay consistent with prior party scenes

proposed.ja: ウェットTシャツコンテスト

terms.gloss: Footraces / drunken dashes across Palace Square in St Petersburg
terms.why_hard: Дворцовая is Palace Square, not a street named Dvortsovaya; 'races' vs 'runs' needs one choice

proposed.ja: 宮殿広場での駆けっこ

terms.gloss: Palace Square (Dvortsovaya ploshchad), the main square by the Winter Palace
terms.why_hard: Must not become 'Palace Street' or a generic palace courtyard

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte
terms.why_hard: Surname-only vs full name must match the book's established style

terms.gloss: Napoleon Hill (Think and Grow Rich) and Paul Graham (startup essays)—the two stylistic models named
terms.why_hard: Bare surnames; Hill/Graham could be anyone; Graham is Paul Graham of Y Combinator, not Billy Graham

terms.gloss: Cuttable manifesto-like passages from his posts
terms.why_hard: манифестационный is not 'manifestation'; it's manifesto-tone, not occult manifestation

proposed.ja: マニフェスト調の断片

terms.gloss: Yank out / cherry-pick fragments (slightly contemptuous)
terms.why_hard: Too literary or too crude both miss the scrap-harvesting sense

terms.gloss: Scraps/tatters of text used as raw material for generated new texts
terms.why_hard: Don't upgrade to 'fragments' if the book keeps the rag-scrap image elsewhere

terms.gloss: Biblical 'old wineskins' (Matthew 9:17): obsolete vessels that new wine will burst
terms.why_hard: Literal 'decrepit bellows/wineskins' without the Gospel echo reads as nonsense

terms.gloss: New vinedressers/winemakers who must wait for the new wine—continuation of the wineskin parable
terms.why_hard: виноградарь is vinedresser, not generic 'grape growers' or 'new vintners' if the parable is lost

proposed.ja: 新しいぶどう園の働き手

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte, subject of the book
terms.why_hard: Name transliteration differs per language (Дуров/杜罗夫/ドゥロフ) and must match the whole book

terms.gloss: The Ritz-Carlton hotel on Tverskaya in Moscow, near Red Square
terms.why_hard: Later 'в том же Ritz' refers back to an earlier Petersburg/Moscow meeting; must keep identical form across segments

terms.gloss: Durov jokingly treated as a totem, an object of cult veneration the author will 'interrogate'
terms.why_hard: Ironic elevation of Durov; a literal translation loses the mock-shamanic awe

terms.gloss: Allusion to the film 'The Matrix' — the phone call offering a new life (red pill moment)
